title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-07
content:
Daily on-call scratchpad (Lena) - 2026-03-07

Summary:
- Overnight paging: 03:12 UTC spike in token-serving latency for /v1/generate on prod-west; alert fired (p95 > 450ms).
- Pager: woke up at 03:18, triaged with Noah. Brief mitigation applied (route B fallback to smaller model variant), latency returned to baseline by 03:45.
- Root cause suspected: sudden surge of long-seq requests from customer account acct-phi-22 (batching + long prompt combos) + degraded node in GPU pool (OOM thrashing).

Timeline / notes:
- 03:12 Alert: p95 token latency > 450ms across model-route-prod-west. Alert group: latency/token-p95-prod-west.
- 03:15 Slack: notified #sre-oncall, routed to Noah (primary) and me (secondary).
- 03:18 SSH into runner logs (gpu-node-17). Observed repeated OOMs and container restarts (kube evictions).
- 03:22 Checked autoscaler: pool had scaled up but new nodes slow to join due to image pull backoff (registry throttling).
- 03:25 Applied temporary routing policy: route heavy seq requests to model-small-v2 (route B) as fallback. Added 10s request timeout at edge for large requests.
- 03:31 Metrics: p95 dropped to ~210ms. Error rate normalized.
- 03:45 Confirmed customer team (acct-phi-22) throttled on their side and we removed fallback.
- 04:10 Follow-up: filed INC-4821 to track hardware eviction + registry backoff.

Immediate follow-ups (high priority):
- [ ] INC-4821: Investigate root cause of OOM thrashing on gpu-node-17 (assign to Infra on-call) - link JIRA-INC-4821.
- [ ] Check registry usage patterns / rate limits with cloud provider; ask infra to raise pull throughput or pre-pull critical images to nodes. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-09.
- [ ] Add a temporary autoscaler emergency workaround to pre-warm instances when p95 > 300ms for >5m. (low-risk knob) Owner: Noah. Due: 2026-03-08.

Runbook TODOs (things to add/update):
- [ ] Update runbook: "GPU node OOM" to include image-pull backoff as escalation path (we missed that step).
- [ ] Add checklist entry to latency runbook for checking image-pull/backoff and registry quotas.
- [ ] Document fallback routing playbook for model-small-v2 (when to flip, what telemetry to watch).

Customer comms / post-incident:
- Customer acct-phi-22 alerted via CS at 05:00. They reported a burst of long prompts from one of their jobs. Recommend they: 1) split into smaller seq sizes, 2) add client-side batching cap.
- Drafted short note for CS to send: "We observed transient infrastructure strain caused by concurrent large-sequence requests which triggered container restarts on an affected GPU node; we applied automatic fallback routing to maintain latency and are investigating registry pull backoffs that slowed autoscaler recoveries." (send after infra triage completes)

Logs / evidence to attach to postmortem:
- gpu-node-17 syslog snippets (03:10-03:30) - container OOM events.
- kubernetes events showing imagePullBackOff during scale up.
- Edge metrics: request distribution to route B during mitigation window.
- Slack convo snapshot: #sre-oncall thread at 03:12-03:50.

Ideas for long-term mitigations:
- Proactive image pre-pull for critical inference images in popular regions (warm pool).
- Hardening autoscaler to consider node join time and image pull latency in decision logic.
- Fine-grained per-customer long-seq protection policy (rate limit or circuit-breaker) to prevent blast radius.

Personal notes / quick TODOs:
- [ ] Sync with Infra on Monday (03/09) about registry quotas and pre-pull plan.
- [ ] Follow up on PR for fallback routing metrics (PR 987) - make sure it exposes route-switch tags for tracing.
- [ ] Add a short tutorial in runbook for junior on-call: how to flip model route fallbacks safely.

Open questions:
- Was gpu-node-17 the only node in that AZ experiencing OOMs, or is this a pattern across similar instances? (ask infra for broader scan)
- Can we detect long-seq storm patterns earlier via the edge (before tokens are sent to runtime)?

Notes to self (keep):
- When paging overnight, first step -> check node health + k8s events, then autoscaler, then fallback routing. Keep CS in loop once mitigation is stable.
- Don't flip fallback for >15m without a rollout plan (can mask root cause).

Related artifacts / refs:
- JIRA-INC-4821 (INC created)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABC123/p1612345678900123
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/987

-- Lena
